# Buddy — The Gift Offer + Starter Prompts (Dani)

## The offer note (person-to-person — say it, or paste it in a text/email)
> I made something for you. It's a little helper that answers anything in plain English — the kind of thing you'd rather not have to call someone about. It's free, it's completely yours, and you honestly can't break it. Here — try this first, watch:
>
> *[show them on YOUR screen first — type a real question, let them see the answer appear]*
>
> Want it on your phone? Takes two minutes to set up your own. No charge, ever, and I'm not in it — it's just yours.

**Why this works:** leads with dignity, not "AI." The magic happens before any setup. They feel it before they understand it.

## First-prompt by audience (put ONE real win in front of them — never a blank box)

**USAFA classmate / older friend:**
- "Explain this Medicare/insurance letter in plain English and tell me what to do next." *(paste the letter text)*
- "Write a toast for my granddaughter's wedding — she's a nurse, loves hiking."

**Nonprofit volunteer / lone mission-worker:**
- "Turn these rough notes into a warm thank-you letter to a donor: …"
- "Draft a short paragraph for our grant application about why this program matters."

**Anyone (the universal first win):**
- "Explain this to me like I'm smart but new to it: …"

## The referral spark (give them a one-line forward)
> "My classmate made this — it's free, it's yours, and it'll answer the thing you've been too proud to ask anyone. Here's how to start: [link] — paste this first: 'Explain this letter in plain English.'"

**The rule:** people refer *stories where they were the hero*, not tools. Engineer the first win to be tellable ("it wrote the eulogy I couldn't start"), and make passing it on as easy as forwarding a text.
